# R4: Similar players, value for money and the shortlist

{{logo_html}}

Data: StatsBomb Open Data (github.com/hudl/open-data), used under the StatsBomb Public Data User
Agreement, and transfermarkt-datasets (github.com/dcaribou/transfermarkt-datasets, CC0; built from

crowd-sourced estimates, not transfer fees.

**How to read this page.** Every list below is a *similar profile under stated assumptions*: which
players' {{season_label}} numbers look most like {{target.name}}'s, given the metrics and weights chosen in
`config/similarity.yaml`. It is not a prediction that anyone would succeed at Leicester. Only {{season_label}}
matches and market values on or before 2016-07-01 are used.

Settings fingerprint: `config/similarity.yaml` sha256 `{{config_sha256}}` (written before the first
run on real data and not changed since).

## What this step does, in plain words

1. **Who is compared.** All {{pool.role}}s with at least {{pool.min_minutes}} league minutes in
   {{season_label}}: {{pool.pool}} players including {{target.name}}, who is only the target, never a candidate.
2. **What is compared.** {{n_metrics}} numbers (per 90 minutes, plus pass completion) in four groups, each with a weight that reflects what
   {{target.name}} contributed (reasons in the config). Defensive numbers are adjusted for team
   possession, so a player in a side that rarely has the ball is not flattered.

{{table:weights}}

3. **On one scale.** Each number becomes a z-score within the pool (how many standard deviations above
   or below the pool average), capped at +/-{{settings.clip}} so one extreme number cannot dominate.
   {{pool.clipped_values_pool}} values in the pool were capped; {{pool.clipped_values_target}} of them
   are {{target.name}}'s.
4. **Similarity.** The weighted distance between a player's z-scores and {{target.name}}'s, turned into
   a 0-100 score (100 = identical; 0 = as far apart as the capped scale allows). Distance, not angle:
   a player with half the output in the same proportions is not a replacement. The cosine (profile
   shape regardless of level, 1 = same shape) is shown next to it as a check.
5. **Price.** Transfermarkt market value at 2016-07-01. {{pool.priced}} of the {{pool.candidates}}
   candidates have one; {{pool.unpriced}} do not and appear only in the similarity list.
   {{pool.stale_priced}} priced candidates have a valuation older than 183 days; they stay in, marked
   "stale value".

## Can the profiles be trusted? Split-half check

Each player's season was cut in two at {{stability.split_date}}. For the {{stability.players}} pool
players with at least {{stability.min_minutes_per_half}} minutes in each half, we took his first-half
profile and asked: among all {{stability.players}} second-half profiles, where does his own rank?

{{table:stability}}

Median rank of a player's own second half: {{stability.median_rank}} out of {{stability.players}}.
{{target.name}}'s own second half ranks **{{stability.target_rank}}** of {{stability.players}}.

**What this says, in plain words.** If profiles were pure noise, a player's own second half would be
the closest match {{top1.chance|pct}} of the time and in the top 5 {{top5.chance|pct}} of the time.
It is the closest {{top1.share|pct}} and in the top 5 {{top5.share|pct}} of the time: far above
chance, so the numbers capture something real and repeatable about how each player plays. But it is
far from certain: for the other {{top5_miss|pct}} of players, at least five other players' second
halves look more like them than their own does. Half-season profiles rest on half the minutes of the full-season
ones used for the lists below, so the full-season profiles should be steadier, but the lesson holds:
differences of a point or two in similarity between candidates are within the noise. Treat the
shortlist as a group worth scouting, not as an exact order. {{target.name}} himself is not perfectly
stable either (rank {{stability.target_rank}}), so any candidate's numbers would also vary from one
half-season to the next. {{stab_not_rated}} pool players had fewer than
{{stability.min_minutes_per_half}} minutes in one half and get no split-half rank ("-" in the tables).

## Value for money

**The frontier (no weights).** A player is on the frontier when nobody else in the pool is at least
as similar *and* at least as cheap (and better on one). {{frontier_count}} players are on it, of whom
{{frontier_eligible}} also meet the shortlist constraints. Cheapest first:

{{table:frontier}}

**The shortlist.** Constraints: market value up to EUR {{cap_m}}m (half of {{target.name}}'s own value
of EUR {{target_value_m}}m), age {{settings.age_min}}-{{settings.age_max}} at 2016-07-01, no Leicester
City players. {{pool.eligible}} candidates meet them. The value score is
{{settings.value_weights.similarity}} x similarity percentile + {{settings.value_weights.price}} x
cheapness percentile, both among those {{pool.eligible}}; the top 10:

{{table:shortlist}}

{{shortlist_on_frontier}} of the 10 are on the frontier; {{overlap}} are also in the top 10 by
similarity; {{shortlist_stale}} carry a stale valuation. {{shortlist_no_split}} of the 10 have no
split-half rank (under {{stability.min_minutes_per_half}} minutes in one half), so their profiles
rest on fewer matches and deserve extra care. "Split-half rank" is where a player's own second half
ranked against his first half (1 = most stable).

## What this does not tell us

- Whether a player would fit Leicester's system, team-mates or league; only that his {{season_label}}
  numbers resemble {{target.name}}'s under these weights.
- Anything about fitness, character, wages, a club's willingness to sell or the real fee: market
  values are crowd-sourced estimates.
- How much the lists depend on the weights, minutes threshold, valuation date and budget: that is the
  R5 sensitivity analysis.
